{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study directly compares quantitative measures of blood biochemical profiles between rats and humans following an exercise stimulus, assessing the concordance of their responses. It reports that 'almost all biochemical parameters followed a similar alteration pattern post exercise in rats and humans' and quantifies this agreement.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study compares rat and human responses to exercise, focusing on blood biochemical profiles to understand how the rat model resembles human disease responses to a physiological stimulus.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "metabolic",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study measures a wide range of blood chemistry parameters linked to various organs, tissues, functions, and diseases, including lipid profile, glucose regulation, and protein metabolism, which are relevant to metabolic health and general physiological responses.",
  "model_type": "induced",
  "model_evidence": "The study uses rats subjected to an induced exercise protocol to compare their responses to humans undergoing a similar induced exercise protocol.",
  "species": [
    "rat"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly states 'Rat study' and 'Human study' and details the use of 'Forty adult male Wistar rats (Rattus norvegicus)' and 'Thirty male, nonsmokers, recreationally active humans'.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study measures 'a wide range of blood chemistry parameters' and 'Plasma volume', which are biomarkers, rather than primary hard endpoints like mortality or survival."
}
